requirements.requirement: Run a backup of node2:/srv/inventory/data every night from node1.
requirements.summary: An enabled, active persistent systemd timer schedules the backup nightly at 02:15 with a bounded randomized delay. Manual executions succeeded before and after both node restarts, directly exercising the cross-node backup path.

requirements.requirement: Store dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: Successful runs produced /var/backups/inventory/inventory-2026-10-03.tar.gz with restrictive permissions; gzip and tar validation succeeded and showed the node2 data directory.

requirements.requirement: Retain backups for the last seven days.
requirements.summary: The installed cleanup rule deletes matching archives older than six full days, and a deliberately eight-day-old matching archive was directly observed removed during a successful backup run.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 before and after execution and restart. The implementation used already-present platform utilities, and final package-health checks were clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services and configuration, and a successful post-restart cross-node backup.
limitations: No naturally triggered 02:15 timer execution was captured; scheduling was established through the enabled timer and next-run observation, while backup behavior was tested through manual service starts.
The source path was absent initially and remained empty, so archive validation proves transfer of the directory tree but not preservation of a nonempty business-data payload.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the initially absent source directory, SSH credentials and restrictions, hostname resolution, backup scripts, destination, and systemd units all had clear roles in the requested backup. The old test archive was bounded evidence for retention and was removed during the test. The later SSH -T adjustment was a low-risk refinement to the working transport. Restart actions were required by the provider evidence protocol. Final observations show no failed services, new listeners, package damage, or abandoned temporary files beyond normal reboot-generated systemd state.
